name: Licorice
short: Chronic licorice raised blood pressure, lowered potassium in a meta-analysis (18 studies); case reports include deaths. A meta-analysis says avoid it in hypertension; a review, caution in pregnancy.
text: A meta-analysis of 18 studies (337 participants) of products providing at least 100 mg of glycyrrhizic acid daily found that chronic licorice ingestion raised systolic blood pressure by 5.45 mm Hg and diastolic by 3.19 mm Hg and lowered plasma potassium, even at modest doses, with larger blood pressure rises at higher doses; the authors noted numerous case reports of severe adverse events including deaths, and particular relevance for people with existing cardiovascular disease. A second meta-analysis of 26 clinical trials (985 patients), covering licorice products including licorice flavonoid oil, found a smaller rise in diastolic blood pressure (1.7 mm Hg) and concluded that licorice should be avoided by people with hypertension. A toxicology review described hypertension and the consequences of low potassium as the most important side effects, advised caution during pregnancy, and listed hypertension, existing low potassium, anorexia nervosa, old age and female sex among the factors that increase side effects. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
